transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith... I guess I'm here because of work. The warehouse. It's... the routing system there, it isn't just a regular computer to me anymore. I've been operating the trucks there for a long time, you know? Back when I started, we just used paper manifests. My old manager, Gary, he used to keep everything on this battered yellow legal pad. Gary was a real character—he actually won a few thousand on a scratch-off ticket once and bought a used Corvette. Bright red. Always parked it way in the back so nobody would ding the doors. 

But, uh, what was I saying? Right, the new system. I know it's been marking my moves. Every time I beep a barcode, it's sending these messages through the scanners, communicating, trying to push me out because I'm one of the old hands. They want the older guys gone. Which reminds me, I need to take my own truck in for an oil change soon, the check engine light came on Tuesday when I was pulling into the employee lot, and I just haven't had the time to get under the hood...
You mentioned the scanner is communicating with you; do you actually hear voices coming from the scanner, or is it more of a feeling that it is sending you messages?

It's... it's actual voices, Dr. Smith. It's not just a feeling. It started at the warehouse, but now... now it doesn't even matter where I am. Even when I'm just sitting out in my garage, you know, with the doors pulled down and the engine shut off, I hear them. Clear as day. It's the dispatch voices. They call out my operator number over and over, saying I'm dangerous, saying security is coming to get me. 

My garage used to be my quiet place, you know? I've got this old workbench in there that belonged to my father-in-law. Solid oak. He built it himself back in the seventies before he lost his sight. He was a carpenter, a real craftsman. Made these beautiful birdhouses, too—intricate little things with shingles and everything. We had one hanging in the oak tree out back for years until a storm knocked it down in '08. That was a bad storm, took down power lines all over the county. We were eating canned beans over a camp stove for three days. My wife—God rest her soul—she made a game out of it, pretending we were pioneers... 

But anyway, yeah. The voices. They just keep calling my number, telling me they're coming for me, even when I'm just sitting there at that oak workbench in the dead quiet.
How long have you been hearing these voices from the dispatchers?

Well, let's see... it's been a while now. I'd say the voices and, you know, all this stuff with the scanners and them trying to push me out, it's been going on for about a year and eight months. Almost two years. It started right around the time they brought in those new electric pallet jacks. 

Man, those things are quiet. Too quiet, if you ask me. You used to be able to hear a forklift coming from three aisles over, you know? The hum of the propane, the clanking. Now, these young kids zip around corners on those electric ones, not even honking the horn. Almost took my toes off twice in one week. And they wear those ear pods while they drive! We'd have been fired on the spot back in Gary's day for having headphones on the floor. Gary was strict about safety. He used to make us watch these terrible safety videos from the eighties, the ones where the actors would dramatically fall off a loading dock in slow motion. We'd always laugh, but he meant well. 

But yeah, anyway, the dispatch voices... it's been about a year and eight months since they started calling my number.

Aside from hearing these voices, have you noticed any other changes in how you think, like difficulty organizing your thoughts, or have you found it harder to take care of your daily routines, like grooming or eating, since this started?

Well, it's funny you ask about getting mixed up, because lately, yeah, I do get real turned around. At work, and even sometimes when I'm just at home, I get so mixed up that I'll just stand there holding my hands out in front of me, like they're still on the forklift controls, you know? And I'll be repeating this same safety phrase over and over, out loud, while folks are just standing there trying to talk to me. 

It's like I'm stuck on a loop. Speaking of loops, I used to collect these old reel-to-reel tapes. Had a whole setup in the basement. I found this one tape at a garage sale out in Springfield—guy wanted two bucks for it, but I talked him down to a dollar. Turns out it was an old radio broadcast from 1964, a local baseball game. The announcer had this incredible voice, real deep and smooth. I used to listen to it on Sundays while I was polishing my boots. I always bought Red Wing boots. They cost a pretty penny, but if you take care of the leather, they'll last you a decade. You gotta use the mink oil, though, not that cheap silicone spray. The silicone dries out the stitching... 

But anyway, yeah, I just stand there holding my hands like I'm driving the lift, saying the safety words over and over. It's like my brain just stalls out.
